title: Prison (Genesis 39–40)
hookLine: a false accusation, prison, and a forgotten favor

lines: A CLOAK LEFT IN HER HAND.
cards: Egypt. Joseph is a slave now, still a young man, bought by an officer of Pharaoh named Potiphar. And something odd happens: everything he touches goes well.

Soon he's running the whole house. Then his master's wife starts noticing him, day after day, and one day, when no one else is inside, she grabs him by his cloak. He runs, and leaves the cloak in her hand.
She holds up the cloak and says he attacked her: the second time Joseph's clothes have been turned into a lie, after the coat in goat's blood. Potiphar believes her. Joseph goes to prison.

teach.h: THE LORD WAS WITH JOSEPH, IN THE CELL.
teach.b: Read chapter thirty-nine slowly and one phrase keeps coming back: the Lord was with Joseph.

teach.h: HE SAID NO WHEN NO ONE WAS WATCHING.
teach.b: It's there when he's a slave in Potiphar's house, when his master sees everything prospering in his hands, and twice in the prison.

"But the Lord was with Joseph," the Douay-Rheims reads, and soon the keeper of the prison puts him in charge of the other prisoners. Not on the day he's made governor: in the slave quarters and the cell.
The text never says God got him out. It says God was with him in it. Second, what Joseph does when no one is looking.
He refused his master's wife with two reasons: it would betray the man who trusted him with everything, and it would be a sin against God. Nobody was watching. That was the whole test.
Third, the forgotten favor. Two of Pharaoh's officials land in the same prison: the chief butler, who poured Pharaoh's wine, and the chief baker. Each has a dream.
One morning Joseph sees their sad faces and asks why. Interpretations belong to God, he says, then tells them: in three days the butler goes back to his post, and the baker dies. Both come true.
Joseph asks the butler one thing: remember me to Pharaoh. And the chapter ends flatly. The butler forgot him.
Centuries later, a psalm remembers this stretch: his feet humbled in fetters, iron around him, until God's word came. The chapter doesn't hurry past the waiting, and it never calls it wasted.

how: The Joseph story is read at Mass on a weekday in Lent, and Psalm 105 (104 in the Douay numbering), which remembers Joseph in fetters, is among the psalms of the Liturgy of the Hours.

o: the punishment Joseph earned for his pride
where Joseph waited until his brothers came
where Joseph lands on a false charge, God with him

games.q: who's who in the prison — tap the pairs.
p: left in his master's wife's hand
his dream ended in his death

s: the text says God got Joseph out of prison quickly
it says the Lord was with Joseph in prison. he stayed, and two more years passed after the butler forgot him.
Joseph says interpretations belong to God
before he hears the two dreams, he hands the meaning back to God.
the butler remembered Joseph as soon as he was free
the chapter ends flatly: the butler forgot him.

games.q: you're Joseph in prison. the butler's dream came true, just as you said, and he's going back to Pharaoh's court. what do you ask him?
o: remember me to Pharaoh, and get me out of here.
a share of whatever reward he gets.
games.why: he asks the butler to remember him and mention him to Pharaoh. the chapter's last line: the butler forgot him. two full years pass.

practice: Find one moment in your day that nobody's checking, the dishes in the sink, a receipt slightly wrong in your favor, what you say about someone who isn't there, and picture doing the right thing in it, quietly, with no audience.
If you pray, carry the chapter's phrase, the Lord was with Joseph; if you don't, just hold the choice and let it settle.

wordCard.voice: Prison. In Genesis, the place Joseph lands on a false charge, and where the text says, twice, the Lord was with him. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: the prison in Joseph's story. the word sohar is rare outside these chapters, and its exact sense is uncertain.

carryVoice: Your line: the lord was with joseph. Not after the cell, but in it. See you tomorrow.
